clue.text: Bringing affability, listen to tragic woman outside home

parts.note: to listen is to hear

indicators.note: the woman's name is placed around the word for home, enclosing it

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Hardy's tragic heroine
IN means at home

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful hears out a tragic woman outside her house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing' is only a link word; Hardy's Tess is the standard crossword tragic woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartiness is warm, cordial friendliness, a close synonym for affability.

clue.text: Spirit not good in the army

indicators.note: not means the letter for good is left out of the spirit word

parts.note: a ghost is a spirit

explanation.surface: A ghostly presence that is no good haunts the military.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a large body of people, especially an army in old usage, as in the heavenly host.

clue.text: Publicise drink in a place with lounges for travellers?

definitions.text: a place with lounges for travellers?

parts.note: to air something is to make it public
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a drink seen in a departure lounge.
explanation.definitionFit: Departure lounges for passengers are a feature of every airport, so this descriptive definition fits.

clue.text: Feeling resentful when there's removal of barrier

definitions.meaning: being upset or put out by a slight
read as taking off a fence, i.e. removing a barrier

explanation.definitionFit: To take offence is to feel resentful; split differently the phrase becomes taking off a fence.

clue.text: Attacker finally entering what is an island?

definitions.text: Attacker finally entering what is an island?

indicators.note: the last letter goes inside the phrase, as an invader enters a land

parts.note: John Donne wrote 'No man is an island', so the thing that would be an island is NO MAN

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word attacker

explanation.surface: An invader lands on an island, perhaps Britain itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The R ending 'Attacker' enters NO MAN; the whole clue then describes the Normans, who invaded the island of Britain in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans were attackers who invaded and conquered the island of Britain in 1066.

clue.text: European resort gets to empty after upset

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word for empty upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: to drain is to empty

explanation.surface: A holiday resort ends up having to be emptied after some trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' looks like an adjective, but it names a person here, a native of one country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spaniard is a native of Spain, a European country.

clue.text: Report of seaweed in rock

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the seaweed's name is spoken aloud

parts.note: laver is an edible seaweed, used in Welsh laverbread

explanation.surface: A survey notes seaweed growing in a rock pool.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent LAVER and LAVA sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Lava is molten rock from a volcano, which solidifies into rock itself.

clue.text: Marshal in a cowboy's patch reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is said aloud to give a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a range is open grazing land where cowboys work, so a range

explanation.surface: A US marshal patrols a cowboy's territory in a western.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' looks like a western lawman, but it is the verb meaning to put in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal people or ideas is to arrange them in order, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Ennoble any silly person finding a monarch's favour

indicators.note: silly suggests the words are muddled foolishly into a new order

explanation.surface: A king raises a foolish courtier to the peerage to please himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Boleyn won Henry VIII's favour and became his second wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Boleyn caught the eye of King Henry VIII and became his queen, an example of royal favour.

clue.text: Perhaps a match player likely to score goal

definitions.meaning: a match is one example of a thing struck to light it
a footballer whose job is to score, a forward

explanation.definitionFit: A match is a striker since it is struck to light; a striker is also the attacking football player.

clue.text: Hot dog?

parts.note: not the sausage snack but a firedog, a metal support that sits in a fireplace and gets hot

explanation.definitionFit: An andiron is a firedog, a metal bracket holding logs in a hearth, so literally a hot dog.

clue.text: Grid not nice, empty clues -—- terribly off-putting

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters are mangled into a new arrangement
empty means the inside of the word clues is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A solver complains that an ugly grid with thin clues is very discouraging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves CS from 'clues'; with GRIDNOTNICE those letters are rearranged by 'terribly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disconcerting unsettles or disturbs you, which is what off-putting means.

clue.text: Leap to the stars? There must be limits!

parts.note: to bound is to leap
Aries is a constellation and star sign, standing for the stars of astrology

explanation.surface: An ambitious leap towards the heavens is met with a warning about limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Boundaries are the limits or edges that mark where something ends.

clue.text: Roll around the centre

indicators.note: around means the word for roll is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a bun is a bread roll

explanation.surface: Someone turns a bread roll round to find its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The nub is the core or central point of a matter, so a synonym for centre.

clue.text: A bit of stuff lying in grass

indicators.note: the word for stuff lies inside the word for grass

parts.note: to grass is to inform, which is also to sing to the police
matter is stuff, material

explanation.surface: A small piece of material is found lying in a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass and sing are both British slang for informing to the police, which is why one stands for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a small amount or slight knowledge, so a bit.

clue.text: Dull boy goes to school officer

parts.note: mat or matt means dull, not shiny
Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boring lad becomes an official at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A matron is the senior nurse or housekeeper at a British boarding school, one of its officers.

clue.text: Wooded or arable ground?

indicators.note: ground, as in ground down or crushed, means the letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A question of whether some land is forested or farmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun for land, but it is the past tense of grind, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreal means relating to trees, so a wooded place is arboreal in character.

clue.text: Medicinal powder one woman fed to another

indicators.note: one name is fed into the middle of the other

parts.note: Mia is another woman's name
Agnes is a woman's name

explanation.surface: One woman gives another a dose of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesia is magnesium oxide, a white powder used as an antacid and laxative medicine.

clue.text: Sporting contest with pulling power

parts.note: a contest won by heaving on a rope, where pulling power is literally the strength to pull

explanation.definitionFit: Tug of war is a team sport in which two sides pull a rope, so pulling power decides it.

clue.text: Fight starts to get rough —- explanation for terrible fall

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: eating the apple caused the Fall of Man in Genesis

explanation.surface: A brawl turns nasty after someone takes a heavy fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'terrible fall' is the biblical Fall, blamed on the apple from the tree of knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple is to wrestle or struggle at close quarters, to fight.

clue.text: Disorganised hovel beast sits in

indicators.note: the animal sits inside the hovel word

parts.note: a sty is a filthy dwelling, a hovel
a cat is a beast, an animal

explanation.surface: A muddled scene: an animal lounging in a squalid shack.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty is British informal for scatterbrained, absent-minded and disorganised.

clue.text: Shake medicine initially — pour it into very large whisky!

indicators.note: the letter is poured into the measure of whisky

parts.note: a treble is a triple measure of spirits

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of medicine

explanation.surface: A shaky patient tops up a huge whisky with medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pour it into' puts M inside TREBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tremble is to shake involuntarily, as from fear or cold.

clue.text: Sets up nothing right, being in a dazed state

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for sets is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to set something is to put it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone sets up nothing properly because they are befuddled.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near-unconsciousness or bewilderment, a daze.

clue.text: What comes with the Queen acceding initially?

definitions.text: What comes with the Queen acceding initially?

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of acceding

explanation.surface: Asking what arrives when a new queen takes the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, the clue says a new era begins when a queen accedes to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Each new reign begins a new era, so an era is what comes with a monarch's accession.

clue.text: Horse unable to run could be such a pudding, say?

definitions.meaning: a racehorse that does not take part, one that fails to start

definitions.text: could be such a pudding, say?
definitions.meaning: a pudding is a dessert, not the first course of a meal

explanation.definitionFit: A horse that fails to start a race is a non-starter; a dessert is literally not a starter course.

clue.text: What sounds like empty-headed streak

indicators.note: the clue openly signals a word that is said the same as another

parts.note: vain can mean foolish or empty, here conceited and shallow

explanation.surface: Asking what a thoughtless, shallow streak in someone resembles.
explanation.definitionFit: A vein is a streak or seam, as of ore in rock or a vein of humour.

clue.text: My claim as a journalist to have influence

parts.note: I'M is the claim 'I am'
the press means journalists collectively

explanation.surface: A reporter boasts that being in journalism gives power.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as I'M PRESS, a journalist's claim to belong to the press.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to make a strong mark on, to have an effect or influence on someone.

clue.text: Elastic apt to go after initial pressure

indicators.note: the synonym for apt is placed after the single letter
initial picks the first letter of the word pressure

parts.note: apt and liable both mean likely or inclined

explanation.surface: Elastic tends to give after a first squeeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliable means easily bent or flexible, which is what elastic describes.

clue.text: Energetic type or one on the way out losing heart?

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a goner is someone doomed, on the way out

explanation.surface: Is someone full of energy, or a dying person who has lost courage?
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' removes N, the middle letter of GONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A goer is a lively, energetic person, informal British usage.

clue.text: Oceanographers letting out "Oops!" having got tangled in seaweed

indicators.note: letting out means the letters of the exclamation are released from the longer word
tangled means the remaining letters are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: Ocean scientists cry out as they become entangled in seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O, O, P, S from OCEANOGRAPHERS and rearrange CEANGRAHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Carragheen is Irish moss, an edible red seaweed used to make carrageenan.
